chunks: Your girth is loose and you have put it on the wrong way.
Nevertheless you enjoy in-law kinship and also the right to ask,
and since you have asked, listen.
As regards the oppression against us in this matter although we were the highest as regards descent and the strongest in relationship with the Messenger of Allāh.
It was a selfish act over which the hearts of people became greedy, although some people did not care for it.
The Arbiter is Allāh and to Him is the return on the Day of Judgement.

key_terms.الْمَقامِ: The position / The station (referring to Caliphate/Imamate)
key_terms.بَنُو أَسَدَ: Banū Asad, a clan of the Prophet's family (Bani Hashim is a sub-clan, but Aqil is often addressed in relation to the broader clan structure or specifically as brother; here referring to familial relation)

ai.seo_question: What is Imam Ali's argument regarding the legitimacy of his leadership versus the usurpation by others?
ai.summary: In this letter to his brother Aqil, Imam Ali (AS) articulates the core Shia grievance of *al-Ishtighal* (usurpation), contrasting the Ahl al-Bayt's superior lineage and covenant with the Prophet against the political ambition of the Sahaba. He characterizes the caliphate's seizure not merely as a political shift but as a spiritual failure where 'greed' (*shahwah*) overcame the nobility of the early community, establishing the theological basis for the Imamate's divine right. This narrative underscores the transition from prophetic authority to the era of the Caliphs, framing Ali's patience as a strategic delay for the eventual establishment of justice.
